sun.upright:
This card belongs to your sign. It covers the last ten degrees of Aries, the stretch Venus rules, so an Aries Sun drawing it is being shown a corner of itself it doesn't visit much. Most of Aries is Mars, the start, the push, first one through the door. The final decan is where Venus gets a say, and Venus is in detriment in your sign, a long way from home, having to work against the grain to be heard. What she wants is simple enough. Company. Some pleasure. The thing you built, with people standing in it.

Fire on fire doubles everything, so when you do stop to celebrate, it's loud and quick and generous, and then it's over and you're on to the next job. I've seen this a lot with Aries Suns. The pride is in the doing, and the moment something's finished it stops feeling like yours. The Emperor is your sign's Major, a man on a stone throne who built the kingdom and sits in it looking stern. Venus's Major is The Empress, leaning back on cushions in a field of wheat, enjoying herself. This card is asking which of the two you'd rather be at the end of a big year, and to be honest you could do with a bit of both.

At work it's the project that shipped last month that nobody marked, you included. At home it might be the place you finally got sorted, or a relationship that's reached moving in or making it official. Before you start the next thing, put a date in the diary to celebrate the last one, and invite the people who helped.
sun.reversed:
Upside down, this card often finds an Aries Sun who's stopped counting wins. The milestone came and went and you were already on the phone about the next job. Or it runs the other way, and you've thrown the party too early, announced the business before it has a customer, told everyone about the house before the loan came through. Venus in detriment struggles to get a word in, and Mars fills the silence with speed.

At work it looks like a string of launches and no feeling of having arrived anywhere. In the body it's a tiredness you keep outrunning. A partner might say you're never really home, even when you're sitting on the couch. Pick the last thing you actually finished and tell someone about it properly, how long it took and what it cost you, and let them be pleased for you.

moon.upright:
Anger's the easy one for an Aries Moon. It comes up hot, gets said, and it's gone by dinner. Tenderness is harder. This card is the Venus decan of your own Moon sign, the tail end of Aries, and Venus is badly placed there, in detriment, far from the signs she rules. So the soft, wanting-to-be-looked-after part of you exists. It just tends to come out sideways, as impatience, or as a sudden urge to get everyone round for a barbecue.

With the card and your Moon both fire, it all runs hotter. When you feel safe with people you feel it fast and completely, the whole-body relief of walking into a house where everyone's pleased to see you. When you don't, you get restless and a bit sharp, and it's tempting to go and do something physical until it passes. That works for a while. Mars rules your Moon and likes to burn things off. Venus would like you to stay in the room and let someone be kind to you, which for an Aries Moon can feel oddly exposing, like being told to sit still at the doctor's.

It shows at home, especially after a hard stretch, when what you need is a meal with your people and you keep booking things instead. It shows in sleep, which goes better after an evening with company than after a late session at the gym. With a partner it's letting them fuss over you. Next time you're wound up, ring a friend, go round, and stay for dinner.
moon.reversed:
When the card is reversed, an Aries Moon can go looking for comfort and then walk out on it. You want company, you get it, and within half an hour you're itchy and making excuses. Or you pick a fight with the person you most wanted to see, because a row feels more familiar than being held. Venus is struggling in your Moon's sign anyway, and a reversed Four can leave home feeling like somewhere you pass through on the way to the next thing.

It tends to show in a house full of people you love that still feels unsettled, and in short, broken sleep after a day spent running. A friend might mention they only ever see you in a rush. Stay for the whole evening next time someone has you over, washing up included, and notice when the itch to leave goes quiet.

rising.upright:
Aries rising tends to come in fast, shoulders first. Mars rules your chart, and strangers usually clock you within a minute as direct, energetic, possibly a bit much. This card is Aries too, from the final ten degrees, the part of your sign Venus looks after. So your own Ascendant is showing its softer side, and people are likely to meet someone warmer than they expected. Friendly. Pleased to see them. Already suggesting drinks.

Venus sits in detriment in Aries, uncomfortable, and on the Ascendant that comes across as charm running at Mars speed. You'd like everyone to get along and you'd like it sorted by Friday. Fire meeting fire makes it catch, and most rooms respond, but some people need longer to warm up than you're giving them. You might notice the quieter ones hanging back while you're three stories in. There's nothing wrong with the warmth. It just tends to arrive before the other person has had time to decide they want it, and Aries rising doesn't always wait for the answer.

It helps in a new workplace, where you'll know everyone's name by Wednesday, and at a wedding or a family party, where you'll be good at pulling strangers into one conversation. On a first date it can come across as keen, which is fine if they like keen. In the next group you walk into, ask one quiet person a proper question and wait through the pause.
rising.reversed:
With the card reversed, the warm entrance can get switched on and left on. You're bright and friendly at the door and exhausted by the time you're back in the car, because a lot of it was effort. Aries rising doesn't love admitting it's tired. Or the welcome goes the other way, rushed and a bit pushy, the hug before the handshake, the invitation to your place on the first day, and people take a step back.

It turns up in a new workplace as a first fortnight where you're everyone's mate, followed by a second month where you feel oddly outside. It turns up at parties you arrive at loudly and leave early. Your face gives it away by the end of the night. Go to the next thing planning to talk properly to three people, and leave when you want to.

sun.upright:
Venus is your Sun's ruler, so when the Four of Wands turns up for a Taurus Sun, the card's planet is walking into its own house. That gives it real authority with you. Taurus is fixed earth, and what you want to be proud of is the life you've built slowly, the home that's properly comfortable, the garden that took years, the savings nobody knows about. This card is about the day you let people in to see it.

The odd part is the card's sign. It's Aries, the sign right before yours on the wheel, and the two of you share almost nothing. Aries is quick. Taurus isn't. Fire and earth don't clash, but they don't click on their own either, and you may feel the card hurrying you. Something's finished and it wants a party, and your instinct is to wait until it's really finished, until the paint's dry and the couch has arrived and there's enough of the good wine. That instinct is usually right about houses. With people it tends to mean they wait a long time for the invitation. The Hierophant is Taurus's Major, the card of doing things the proper way, and the proper way can mean the celebration never happens.

At work this could be a promotion or a long job finally coming good, where you'd happily just keep going. At home it's the renovation or the move. With money it can be the moment to spend a bit on marking something instead of saving all of it. Set a date for the gathering before you feel ready, and keep it.
sun.reversed:
Reversed for a Taurus Sun, the Four can mean a good life with the door shut. You've made the place lovely and nobody sees it. The celebration keeps being put off, first because things aren't ready, then because it's been so long it would feel strange to start. Venus rules Taurus and likes comfort, and with the card upside down comfort starts to mean not being disturbed.

It shows in a home you're proud of and rarely share, and in a milestone at work that slid past because making a fuss felt awkward. Sometimes it's money, spent on the house and not on the people in it. Friends may have stopped asking. Aries is the sign next door to yours, and its hurry is the useful influence here. Ring two people, pick a Saturday, and have them over even if the place isn't quite how you want it.

moon.upright:
A Taurus Moon settles through the body. The same pillow, a hot shower, food that tastes of something, a person sitting close enough to touch. Venus rules Taurus, so your Moon lives in a sign run by the very planet this card belongs to, and when this card is drawn for your tides it's speaking to a need you already know well. You want to be comfortable, with your people, somewhere that feels like it's yours.

The awkward bit is the card's Aries side. Aries sits right next to Taurus and has almost nothing in common with it, and fire and earth only get on once they've been introduced. So the warmth this card brings can feel a bit fast for you. A spontaneous invitation, a house suddenly full, a partner who wants to go out when you'd planned a night in. You might like it once you're there. Taurus Moons often do. It's the switch from settled to social that feels rough, because your body likes some warning before anything changes.

Home is the obvious place this shows, maybe a move that's finally starting to feel like yours, or a kitchen that's become where everyone ends up. The body's another, especially sleep and appetite, which both improve when there's company in the house. With family it can be an old ritual, the Sunday roast, the birthday cake one person always makes. Pick one of those rituals and do it properly, with the good plates.
moon.reversed:
With the card upside down, a Taurus Moon can dig in. You're comfortable, or at least used to things, and an invitation to anything new feels like an attack on the couch. Venus is at home in your Moon's sign and she likes her comforts, so it's easy to call the staying in self-care when it's closer to hiding. A grudge can settle in the same way, quietly, and just stay.

This tends to show in food and sleep, the extra helping, the long lie-in that doesn't help, and in a home where nobody's been over for months. A friend who used to ring may have stopped ringing. It can show with family too, an old hurt about who got invited to what and who didn't. Say yes to the next invitation that comes in, and go for at least an hour.

rising.upright:
The picture on this card is a front gate with flowers tied over it, and Taurus rising is good at gates. You tend to come across as calm and pleasant, easy to be near, with an unhurried warmth people trust before they know why. Venus rules your chart and she's the card's planet too, so drawing the Four of Wands for your mask is about as natural a match as it gets. People are likely to find you welcoming. You may be the one they end up standing next to at the party because it feels safe there.

Its sign is Aries, though, the sign before yours, and the two have very little in common. Earth and fire need introducing. So there's a quicker, hotter note in how you're coming across, more spark than usual, and you might catch yourself saying yes to things fast and then wanting to slow them down. That can surprise people who know you. It can surprise you. The instinct to make any room comfortable is still there, you're just doing it with more urgency, like a host who's worried the food's going cold.

At work it can show in how you greet new people, the tour of the office, the coffee you bring them on day one. On a first date you might be warmer earlier than usual. Hosting is the other obvious place, especially a housewarming or a family event. When you notice yourself speeding up to please a room, finish your sentence at your own pace.
rising.reversed:
Upside down on a Taurus Ascendant, the card can make you look settled to the point of closed. You're polite, the room's comfortable, and nobody quite gets in. Venus rules your chart and likes things just so, and with the Four reversed that can harden into a front that's pleasant and fixed, the same smile whatever anyone says.

New people may come away thinking you're lovely and not sure they met you. You might host a beautiful dinner and not enjoy a minute of it. Sometimes it's the reverse, a rushed friendliness that doesn't suit you, the Aries hurry pushing through a sign that likes to take its time, and people can feel the strain in it. Next time someone new asks how you are, give them the real answer, even if it's only a sentence.

sun.upright:
Gemini Suns are proud of their range. The people you know, the things you can talk about, the way you can walk into any room and find the thread. Mutable air, ruled by Mercury. The Four of Wands and Gemini get on well. Aries is two signs from yours, a sextile, the friendly angle, and air fans fire. So there's no fight here. The card's warmth catches on your sociability and spreads.

Venus is only a visitor in Gemini, with no special standing, and she picks up the local manner, which here means Mercury's. Belonging comes to you through conversation. The group chat that turns into an actual dinner. The introduction you made three years ago that became a marriage. What the card asks your Sun is whether any of that has a home base. A Gemini can know two hundred people and still not have the four who'd help them move house. A sextile is an open door, and you still have to walk through it. The Lovers is Gemini's Major, a card about choosing, and choosing who your people are is harder for you than you let on.

At work this can look like the team you've pulled together, or a project that finally lands and deserves more than a thumbs-up emoji. With friends it's picking a regular night and sticking to it. It might also be a sibling or an old friend you'd like to be closer to. Choose four people and have them over, and then do it again next month.
sun.reversed:
Plans are how the reversed Four usually shows up for a Gemini Sun. There's always a get-together being talked about, a reunion, a trip, a housewarming for the flat you moved into last year, and very few of them happen. Mercury rules Gemini and can make talking about a thing feel almost like doing it. Venus picks up the habit.

With friends it's a lot of 'we should' and a calendar that says otherwise. At work you're the one who knows everybody, and not many people know much about you. It can show at home too, where the place still doesn't feel lived in because nobody's been round. Take the plan you've mentioned most often, pick the date, and send an actual invitation with a time on it.

moon.upright:
Talking is how a Gemini Moon feels. You work out what's upset you by saying it out loud, often to three different people, and by the third time it's settled. Mercury rules your Moon, so the nerves are quick and the mind is quicker. The Four of Wands turns up for your tides with a garland strung between four staves and people celebrating behind it, and for you the soothing part is the noise of it, a full table, overlapping conversations, somebody laughing in the kitchen.

Fire and air get on, so the card's warmth doesn't smother you. It lifts you. Aries sextiles Gemini, a cooperative angle, and Venus in your Moon's sign has no special rank, so she borrows Mercury's habits and affection comes through words. A long voice memo from a friend can do as much for you as a hug. What catches people out about Gemini Moons is how tired the quiet makes you. A silent house can feel like something's wrong. The Aries edge in this card makes you want company quickly, and if it isn't there you might fill the gap with your phone, scrolling until one in the morning.

Sleep is where this shows, better after a good talk and worse after an evening alone with a screen. It shows with siblings or cousins, the family chat running warmer than usual. Moving house or changing flatmates can stir it up too. When the evening feels empty, ring someone and talk until the kettle's boiled twice.
moon.reversed:
Reversed on a Gemini Moon, talk becomes a way of not feeling. You're in six conversations and none of them get near the thing that's bothering you. Someone asks how you are and you tell them a funny story. The warmth of the card is still around, the company, the invitations, and you keep it at the level of chatter, because anything closer makes you restless.

It tends to show at night, with a racing head and the phone in your hand, and with a close friend or partner who's noticed you change the subject. It can show at family gatherings where you're the entertainer and go home oddly lonely. Next time someone you trust asks how you're going, answer with one true sentence, then stop talking for a bit.

rising.upright:
Gemini rising gets introduced to people a lot. Mercury rules your chart, and you come across as quick and curious and easy to talk to, the one who's asked three questions before the other person has sat down. With the Four of Wands on your mask, those questions have a warmer purpose. You're pulling people in, finding out who knows who, making two strangers at a party realise they grew up on the same street.

The astrology is on your side. Aries sextiles Gemini, and air feeds a fire, so the card and your Ascendant help each other along. Venus picks up Mercury's style in your sign, so the charm is verbal, the right joke at the right moment, the name remembered from last time. The thing to know is that a sextile only hands you the opening. It's easy for Gemini rising to make a great first impression on forty people and a lasting one on nobody, because you've moved on before anyone got a second conversation with you.

Starting a new job, you'll know the whole floor quickly, and that's useful. At a big family event you might end up as the unofficial host, merging little groups into one. On first dates the look is warm and fun, and it works best when you follow up. After the next event, message two people you met and suggest something specific.
rising.reversed:
Gemini rising with the card reversed can be great company and hard to know. You work the room, you're funny, people like you, and at the end of it nobody could say what you care about. The questions that usually draw people in start keeping them at arm's length, because you're doing all the asking and none of the answering.

Colleagues enjoy you and couldn't tell anyone a single personal thing about you. Dates go well and don't turn into second dates. In a new neighbourhood there are lots of waves over the fence and nobody you'd ring in an emergency. Mercury rules your chart and can keep things moving so fast nothing lands. Next time you're asked a personal question, give a real answer before you ask one back.

sun.upright:
A Cancer Sun builds itself around home. The family you came from, the one you've made, the flat that finally feels safe. So you'd think the Four of Wands, which is more or less a card of homecoming, would be an easy fit. It mostly is. The astrology adds some grit, though. The card's sign is Aries, which squares Cancer, both of them cardinal, both used to starting things their own way. And the card is fire where your Sun is water, the pairing most likely to produce steam.

What that feels like is two ideas of home arguing. The card wants the doors open, the neighbours in, everyone celebrating. Your Cancer Sun wants to know who's coming, whether there's enough food, whether Aunty is going to start on Dad again. Both are fair. What helps is that Venus rules the first ten degrees of Cancer, the Two of Cups, so a bit of this card already lives in your sign, and it's the one-to-one version. Big celebrations go best for you when they grow out of a close bond, two people who then invite everybody. The Chariot, Cancer's own Major, is a driver in armour. This card is asking you to take the armour off for one night.

At home it might be a move, an engagement, a baby, a family event you've been asked to host. At work you probably treat your team like family, and there may be a milestone worth marking there. Let someone else do the hosting this time, and go as a guest.
sun.reversed:
Hosting everything and enjoying none of it is a common way this card turns up reversed for a Cancer Sun. You cooked, you cleaned, you kept apart the people who needed keeping apart, and you went to bed exhausted and a bit cross. Or the doors have closed. A milestone gets played down because being the centre of attention feels exposed, and the square from Aries turns the discomfort into snappishness with the people you love.

Family events are where you'll see it most, especially ones held at your place. It can show with a partner who'd like to celebrate something you keep brushing off, and at work when your team marks a win and you're too busy looking after them to join in. Name one thing you'd like to be celebrated for, and let someone plan it without your help.

moon.upright:
The Moon rules Cancer, so a Cancer Moon feels everything at full volume and remembers most of it. What it needs is a safe place to put all that, a home, a person, a kitchen where nobody's cross. The Four of Wands arrives for your tides with exactly that picture, and it's a lovely thing to be shown. It's also hotter and louder than you might want. Aries, the card's sign, squares Cancer, and its fire runs into your water.

You'll know the feeling. You long for your people to be gathered, and when they are, it can be a lot. The noise, the heat, the one relative who always says something. Big occasions tend to leave a Cancer Moon wrung out, even the happy ones. There's a quieter way into this card, though. Venus rules the Two of Cups, the opening decan of Cancer, so the part of this card that's native to you is the one-to-one bond, two people at a table. And because Venus is only a visitor in Cancer she takes on the Moon's manner, which makes the warmth softer and more nurturing than Aries usually manages.

It shows at home, in the wish to have family over, or in finally feeling settled somewhere after a move. It shows in the stomach and in sleep, both of which go wonky when home feels unsteady. With a parent it might be a warmer visit than usual. Have one person you love round for dinner, and keep it small.
moon.reversed:
When this card sits reversed on a Cancer Moon, the shell tends to close. You want your people close so badly that one wrong comment at a family dinner sends you home early and quiet for three days. The square with Aries makes hurt come up fast and hot, and then the water in you pulls it back under where nobody can see it.

It shows around family occasions you dread and go to anyway, and in a home that doesn't feel settled, maybe because of a move, maybe because of someone in it. Appetite and sleep go off when that happens. It can also show as testing people, going quiet to see who notices. Pick one person you trust and tell them plainly that you've been feeling unsettled, before you go quiet on them.

rising.upright:
Cancer rising tends to arrive carefully. You read the room, work out who's safe, and warm up once you're sure, and strangers usually take you for kind, a little shy, someone with every mood written on their face. The Moon rules your chart. With the Four of Wands drawn for your mask, the kindness is doing more of the talking. People may find you more welcoming than usual, the one who makes them a cup of tea, finds them a chair, asks after their mum.

Aries squares your Cancer Ascendant, which puts some friction into it. The card's fire meets your water, and there's a hotter, quicker note in you that isn't your usual style. You might find yourself inviting people in before you've decided whether you like them, then wanting to pull back. Venus in Cancer picks up the Moon's colour, so the welcome is homely and caring, and the Aries push is what makes it faster than you'd normally go. That isn't a bad thing. Some people you'd have taken months to warm to are worth warming to sooner.

In a new job, you might be the one who notices the new starter eating lunch alone. With a partner's family, your warmth can win people over fast. At home, having people over might come easier. If you invite someone in quickly and then feel the urge to retreat, stay put for another half hour.
rising.reversed:
A reversed Four on Cancer rising can put on a very good welcome and keep the real door shut. You're lovely to newcomers, you remember their names, you offer the biscuits, and they never get any further than that. The Aries square adds an edge, so when someone does push in too quickly you can go cool on them without warning, and they won't know what they did.

It shows with colleagues who feel looked after and kept at a distance, and in friendships that stay at the cup-of-tea stage for years. Your moods can leak through your face and get read as coldness. It can show with a partner's family too, polite on both sides and nobody relaxing. Let one person you like hear something a bit personal from you, earlier than you'd normally allow.

sun.upright:
Leo Suns like a party, and they like being the reason for it. Fixed fire, ruled by the Sun, you want to be proud of what you've made and you want people to see it, and there's nothing shameful in that. The Four of Wands is about as friendly a card as you could draw for your light. Its sign, Aries, trines Leo, four signs apart in the same element, the angle where things flow without much effort. Venus has no dignity of her own in Leo and takes on the Sun's manner, so the warmth here is big and generous and a little theatrical.

That's the good news, and it's real. Two fire signs together turn the volume up. You may be feeling unusually warm toward the people around you, keen to mark something, keen to have everyone round. The catch with doubled fire is that it can get out of hand. The party gets bigger than the occasion, the budget stretches, and somewhere in the middle of it you might notice you're checking whether people are having a good time because of you. Strength is Leo's Major, a woman calmly holding a lion's jaw, and that kind of calm is what keeps this warm without tipping into a show.

At work it's a win you can share with the team, and you'll be good at making them feel part of it. In a relationship it's a milestone, an anniversary, moving in, a proposal, something that wants a bit of ceremony. Throw the celebration, and give the speech about someone else.
sun.reversed:
Upside down for a Leo Sun, the Four can turn a celebration into a stage. It's your birthday or your promotion or your party, and some part of you is counting who came and how loudly they clapped. Or it goes the other way, and a milestone you'd hoped people would notice slides by without anyone saying anything, and you're hurt and too proud to mention it.

It shows at work when someone else's win gets the attention and you go quiet in the meeting. It shows in friendships where you're always the host and never quite relaxed. With a partner, an anniversary that got forgotten might still be sitting heavy. Go to the next thing someone else is celebrating and make them the centre of it, without bringing up anything of your own.

moon.upright:
Being noticed by the people you love is what settles a Leo Moon. It doesn't need to be a crowd. Just your people, looking at you like you matter, a fuss made on your birthday, a friend who says the dinner was the best they've had all year. The Sun rules Leo, and a Sun-ruled Moon runs warm and generous and feels it badly when the warmth isn't returned. For your tides, this card is about as reassuring as they come. Aries trines Leo, both fire, and the garland and the gathered crowd in the picture are the kind of scene that makes you feel safe.

There's a strong pull toward home and your people, and toward being properly celebrated by them. You'll probably get some of that, and it'll carry you for weeks. Leo Moons can live off one good birthday for months. Same-element pairings can overdo things, though. When you need the warmth this much it's possible to lean on the room too hard, to need everyone to be having a good time before you can feel alright. Venus takes on the Sun's tone in Leo, which makes the affection generous and a touch dramatic.

Hosting at home might be the thing, and you'd love it. With a partner it's being made a fuss of and letting yourself enjoy it without checking it's deserved. With children or young relatives it can be play that feels like a party. Tell one person you love exactly what they did that made you feel special, and be specific.
moon.reversed:
A Leo Moon can go sulky when this card lands reversed. The party happened and nobody made the toast you'd hoped for, or a friend forgot, or a partner's attention has been somewhere else for weeks. The trine that usually makes things easy can make you lazy about asking. You expect people to notice, and when they don't, the hurt comes out as pride.

It shows around birthdays and anniversaries, and in a family where you've always been the warm one and now feel taken for granted. Your mood can drain a room without you meaning it to. It can show in sleep, too, lying awake replaying who said what at dinner. Ask plainly for the thing you want, a night out or a phone call, and don't make them guess.

rising.upright:
People notice when Leo rising walks in, whether you want them to or not. The Sun rules your chart, and strangers read you as warm, confident, a bit regal, someone who probably has a good story. The Four of Wands on your mask adds a welcome to the entrance. You're arriving and making room at the same time, pulling people in, making them feel they've turned up somewhere worth being.

Aries trines Leo in the same element, so the card's style and yours run together easily, and the doubled fire makes it bright. Venus borrows the Sun's colour in Leo, so the charm is sunny and a little showy, and most people like it. The thing to notice is how much of the room ends up pointing at you. A welcome this warm can make quieter people feel they're watching a performance. It can also set a standard you then feel you have to meet every time you walk in, which gets tiring by about the fourth event of the month. Strength, Leo's Major, is very quiet about its power.

At a wedding or a family party, you're probably the one who makes it feel like an occasion. In a new job, people will remember meeting you. On a date it's a strong first impression, and it works best if you ask as many questions as you answer. At the next gathering, spend the first ten minutes with whoever looks least comfortable.
rising.reversed:
Leo rising with this card reversed can end up performing the welcome. You come in bright, you do the rounds, you're charming, and it's work. People remember the entrance and can't say much about you afterwards. Sometimes it's the opposite, and you arrive dimmer than usual, quiet because you're not sure of the reception and too proud to go looking for it.

Work functions where you feel you have to be 'on' bring it out, and so do family gatherings where you're expected to bring the energy. Dating can turn into a lot of sparkle and very little of you. The Sun rules your chart, and it doesn't like being dimmed. Go to one thing as an ordinary guest. Arrive on time, stay in one conversation, and leave when you're tired.

sun.upright:
Virgo Suns take pride in doing things well. Mutable earth, ruled by Mercury, you like the job finished properly, the details right, the thing actually useful to someone. The Four of Wands comes in carrying a party, which is a slightly awkward thing to hand you. Its sign, Aries, is five signs from Virgo, a quincunx, which means the two have nothing in common and keep needing small adjustments to rub along. On top of that, Venus is in fall in Virgo. She's uncomfortable here and a bit unheard, and has to find an indirect way to get her pleasure in.

You'll know how that goes. Something good happens, a project done, a qualification passed, and your first thought is what could have been better. Celebrating feels a bit silly, or premature, or like tempting fate. Earth and fire don't fight, but the card's warmth isn't going to reach you by itself either. There is a way in. Venus rules the middle ten degrees of Virgo, the Nine of Pentacles, a card of someone standing in the garden they worked for and enjoying it. That's your version of this card. Pleasure that comes from a job well done, taken quietly, in a place you've made nice.

At work it's the thing you've finished that deserves more than a tick in your planner. At home it might be the garden, the kitchen, the spare room finally sorted. With your health, it's letting the routine include some fun. Mark the next finished job with something you'd never normally spend money on.
sun.reversed:
Virgo Suns with the Four reversed can edit a good thing until there's nothing left to celebrate. You finished the project and now you're fixing it. You moved house and you're repainting the hall before anyone's been over. Venus in fall makes pleasure hard to land at the best of times, and a reversed Four gives you every excuse to postpone it.

At work it sounds like 'it's fine, there's still loads to do', said about a milestone that deserved more. At home it's a place that's always nearly ready for visitors. Sometimes it's the body, a routine so strict it's lost any joy. Mercury rules Virgo and always has one more correction to make. Pick one thing you've finished and leave it exactly as it is for a week, then have someone round to see it.

moon.upright:
A Virgo Moon settles by sorting things out. The drawer tidied, the list done, the small practical help given to someone who needed it. You feel safe when you're useful. The Four of Wands asks your Moon to be on the other end of that, fed and fussed over and celebrated, and it's harder for you than it looks. Venus is in fall in your Moon's sign, uncomfortable and having to go the long way round, and Aries quincunxes Virgo, an angle where nothing lines up easily.

In practice you'll probably end up in the kitchen at your own party. You'll refill the glasses and wipe the bench and feel calmer doing it than you would sitting down. That's fine, and people love you for it. The trouble is when it stops you receiving anything at all. Earth and fire are neutral to each other, so the warmth is there to be had, it just needs you to step toward it deliberately. There's a foothold, too. Venus looks after the Nine of Pentacles, the middle decan of Virgo, which shows someone at ease in a well-kept place of their own. A tidy, calm home is where you'll feel this card most.

It shows in your stomach and your sleep, which both settle when home is in order. It shows with family, maybe in who does the work at gatherings. It can show at work in the colleague who always brings the cake, which is probably you. Next time someone offers to help, give them a real job and go and sit down.
moon.reversed:
The reversed Four can make a Virgo Moon fret its way through anything nice. You're at the dinner and you're thinking about the dishes, the thing you forgot to buy, what someone meant by that comment. Venus in fall and a quincunx between the card's sign and yours mean pleasure keeps slipping out of reach, and worry moves into the space.

This shows in the gut and in sleep, both of which go tight and restless. It can show as a home you won't have people in until it's perfect, and as a voice telling you that you haven't earned a night off. With family it's often doing all the work at a gathering and feeling faintly resentful by the end. Let the house be untidy next time someone visits, and don't apologise for it.

rising.upright:
Virgo rising comes across as capable. Mercury rules your chart, and people meeting you tend to see someone neat, observant, quietly competent, maybe a bit reserved at first. You notice things. The Four of Wands drawn for your mask asks you to lead with warmth, and warmth doesn't come first for Virgo rising. Usefulness does. The card's sign, Aries, quincunxes Virgo, so there's a constant small mismatch between the welcome the card wants and how you'd go about it, and Venus is in fall on your Ascendant, which makes easy charm feel forced.

So you do it your way. You welcome people by having thought of things. The spare phone charger, the dietary requirements, the directions sent the night before. It works. Once fire and earth have been properly introduced, people feel very looked after around you. Venus also rules the Nine of Pentacles, the middle ten degrees of your sign, and that card's style suits you, a welcome that shows in how well the place has been kept. Someone arriving at yours for the first time will probably notice the clean towels before they notice anything you say.

At work it's the onboarding you quietly do better than HR does. At a family event it's being the one who handles the practical side. In dating you can come across as careful, and people may need a hint that you like them. Say one warm thing out loud to someone new before you do anything useful for them.
rising.reversed:
Upside down on Virgo rising, helpfulness can start to look like inspection. You greet people by fixing something, the crooked picture, the wrong date in their email, and they feel assessed more than welcomed. Venus in fall on your Ascendant doesn't help, because the warmth you do feel has a hard time reaching your face. The quincunx keeps you adjusting small things nobody else noticed.

New colleagues rate you and don't quite warm to you. You organise the party and never relax at it. On dates, nerves come out as precision, and the other person can feel checked over. Mercury rules your chart, and people can tell when it's taking notes. Next time you meet someone new, skip the useful comment and ask them something about themselves you don't need to know.

sun.upright:
Venus rules Libra, so the Four of Wands speaks to a Libra Sun with some authority. It's the card's own planet addressing its own sign, the landlord dropping in. Cardinal air, you want to be proud of things that are fair and good-looking and shared, and a lot of who you are gets worked out alongside other people. This card suits that. A celebration is a thing you do together.

The catch is where the card sits. Its sign is Aries, directly opposite Libra, the other end of the same axis. Aries does what it wants and tells people afterwards. Libra checks first. So the card is pushing you, gently, to want something for yourself and say so, which Libra Suns find oddly hard. You're very good at the party that suits everyone. You're less practised at the one that suits you. Air and fire get along, each feeding the other, so the energy between the card and your Sun is good. It's the direction that's the stretch. Justice is Libra's Major, holding the scales steady, and your own side of the scales counts too.

At work it might be a partnership or a joint project reaching a milestone, and you'll be good at making sure everyone gets credit. In love it's often a big moment, an engagement, a wedding, moving in together. It could also be a friendship that's become more like family. Decide what you'd like the celebration to look like before you ask anyone else.
sun.reversed:
For a Libra Sun, the reversed Four often means a milestone you've turned into someone else's event. It's your promotion, and you took everyone to lunch and asked about them the whole time. It's your wedding, and it's been planned around both families' feelings. Venus rules Libra and likes everyone happy, and Aries, the end of the axis that would just say what it wants, has been pushed to the back.

In love it shows around commitments and shared plans. At work it shows in partnerships where your share of the credit has quietly shrunk. Resentment can leak out later in odd, sharp little comments you regret. Say out loud one thing you'd like for yourself from the next shared occasion, and leave it there without softening it.

moon.upright:
Libra Moons need the room to feel right. Everyone getting on, nobody sulking, the conversation flowing, a person beside you to share it with. Venus rules Libra, and she's the Four of Wands' planet, so when this card comes up for your tides it's speaking your Moon's own language. The pleasure of a good gathering, of a home that feels pretty and peaceful, is something you really feel in your body.

The card's sign is Aries, though, opposite Libra, and that's where things get complicated. Aries is blunt and doesn't mind a bit of conflict. Your Moon minds it a lot. So a celebration can feel lovely right up until someone says the wrong thing, and then the whole evening feels ruined to you even if nobody else noticed. Warmth lifts you quickly, because air and fire feed each other, and tension brings you down just as quickly. The Aries side of this card is pointing out, gently, that some friction at a party is normal and the party survives it.

It shows at home, especially if you share it, where small disagreements can sit on you for days. It shows with a partner, and at family occasions where you're the one keeping the peace. It shows in how well you sleep after a nice evening compared with a tense one. At the next gathering, let one awkward moment pass without fixing it and see what happens.
moon.reversed:
Keeping the peace can start to cost a Libra Moon when the Four comes up reversed. You agree to the dinner you don't want to go to, you smooth over the comment that hurt, you smile through the family event and go home flat. Venus rules your Moon and wants harmony, and a reversed Four can mean the harmony is only on the surface.

It shows in a partnership where you've stopped saying what bothers you, and at family gatherings that look lovely in the photos. The body registers it as tiredness after anything social. Aries sits opposite your Moon, and it's the part of you that would just say it. Tell one person one small true thing you've been swallowing, kindly and without an apology.

rising.upright:
Libra rising makes a lovely first impression, and most people who meet you would say so. Venus rules your chart, so you come across as gracious, easy, well put together, someone who makes a conversation feel smooth. This is Venus's card, and on your Ascendant it's very much at home. You'll probably find it easy to welcome people, to make them comfortable, to get a mixed room talking.

Aries is the card's sign, though, and it sits exactly opposite Libra. With Libra rising, Aries is on your Descendant, the cusp of the seventh house, so this card is also saying something about the people you're drawn to and who you're meeting. A quicker, blunter energy is tugging at your polish. Fire and air are on friendly terms, so it doesn't feel unpleasant. It can mean you come across more direct than usual, more willing to say what you want, and people might find that refreshing. It can also mean meeting someone who's all Aries, forthright and fast, who likes you straight away and says so.

At a big party you're the host's best asset, the one who makes sure the awkward cousin gets included. At work you smooth the first week for anyone new. Dating goes well, gracious with a bit of an edge. Next time someone asks where you'd like to eat, name the place.
rising.reversed:
Libra rising with this card reversed can be so pleasant that nobody finds you. You agree, you mirror, you make everyone comfortable, and you walk away without having said one thing you actually think. Venus rules your chart and makes the polish very convincing. Aries, on the far side of your chart, holds the directness you'd need, and it gets saved for the car ride home.

Colleagues like you and overlook you. The people you date may be charmed and still have no idea what you want. With friends it can look like always going along with the plan, even the ones you hate. Being liked by everyone gets tiring when none of them quite know you. Disagree with someone about something small, and let them see it doesn't bother you.

sun.upright:
Scorpio Suns don't do casual. Fixed water, ruled by Mars in the old system, you're proud of the few bonds that go all the way down and fairly wary of everything else. The Four of Wands is a card of open gates and a crowd waving flowers, which isn't really your scene. Its sign, Aries, is five signs from Scorpio, a quincunx, no common ground. Venus sits in detriment in Scorpio, working against the grain, so easy social warmth costs you more effort than it costs most people. And the card's element is fire, yours is water.

There is one odd link. Mars rules both Aries and Scorpio in traditional astrology, so the card's sign and your Sun answer to the same planet. It's why a Scorpio can throw a very good party once they decide to, all in, no half measures. What you'll probably notice is a pull between wanting to mark something important and not wanting to put it on show. Venus also rules the last ten degrees of Scorpio, the Seven of Cups, the card of too many shiny options, and your version of the Four involves picking the real one out of the lot. You don't want a big wedding. You want the right person at a small one.

At work it might be a win you'd rather celebrate with the two people who helped, and that's fine. In love it's a commitment that matters to you far beyond any announcement. With family it can be an old wound softening enough to let people back in. Tell the one person who should know your good news first, in person.
sun.reversed:
A Scorpio Sun with the Four reversed can refuse to celebrate anything in case it gets taken away. The good news stays a secret. The milestone goes unmarked because marking it would be tempting fate, and people who'd have been glad for you never hear about it. Venus in detriment makes warmth hard to trust anyway, and a reversed card gives the suspicion room to grow.

In love it can look like testing a partner to see if they'll stay. At work it's keeping your wins so quiet they start to look like secrets. With friends, a group can start to feel like something you're watching from outside. Tell one person something good that happened to you, and let them be pleased without looking for the catch.

moon.upright:
A Scorpio Moon feels everything at full depth and shows very little of it. You trust slowly, you notice everything, and when you let someone in, it's completely. For your tides the Four of Wands offers a big warm gathering, garlands and a crowd, and your first reaction may be to wonder who's going to be there. Venus is in detriment in your Moon's sign, uncomfortable and working uphill, and Aries quincunxes Scorpio, so this isn't a natural fit. The card's fire and your Moon's water pull against each other, too.

What it tends to feel like is wanting to belong and not wanting to be exposed. A big loud celebration can leave you tired and on guard. A night with one or two people you'd trust with your life can settle you for weeks. Mars rules Aries and, in the old system, Scorpio as well, so there's more heat in your Moon than people guess, and the card can stir it into a sudden hunger for closeness. Venus looks after the Seven of Cups, the final decan of Scorpio, a card about telling the real thing from the fantasy, and that's your way into this one. The people who actually turn up for you are the ones to gather.

It shows in intimacy, and in a partnership that's deepening. It shows at family events, which you might find hard going. It shows in sleep, which improves when you feel safe with someone. Invite the two people you trust most over for dinner, and tell them something real.
moon.reversed:
Scorpio Moons with the card reversed can start watching for betrayal. You want your people near and you check them, quietly, for signs they'll leave. A gathering that should feel warm feels like a room full of possible hurts. Venus in detriment and the card's fire landing on your water both make comfort hard to believe in. The quincunx between Aries and Scorpio keeps you slightly off balance with people, never quite sure where you stand.

It shows in a relationship where jealousy or suspicion has crept in, and at family events that stir up old grudges. It can show in sleep, and in a body that stays tense around people. Sometimes it's simply disappearing for a few weeks. Pick one person who's earned it and let them see you're hurt about something, without testing them first.

rising.upright:
Scorpio rising gives little away on a first meeting. Strangers tend to find you intense, watchful, a bit hard to read, and some of them find that magnetic. Mars rules your chart in traditional astrology. The Four of Wands drawn for your mask asks for a more open front door, which is a real ask. Venus has a hard time in Scorpio, in detriment, working uphill, and the card's sign, Aries, quincunxes yours, so the quick easy welcome of this card doesn't come naturally to your Ascendant. Fire and water don't mix easily either.

What does happen is that when you decide to welcome someone, it lands hard. You don't greet everyone. You greet the person you've picked, properly, and they remember it. Mars ruling both Aries and Scorpio gives your welcome some heat and directness when you do let it out. Venus looks after the Seven of Cups at the tail end of your sign, which suits your style, choosing carefully who gets let in. The card may be asking you to let that choice happen a little faster, because people can't always wait as long as Scorpio rising likes to make them.

In a new job it might mean letting one colleague in within the first month. At a party it's saying hello first, instead of waiting to be approached. In dating it's showing interest before you're certain it's returned. Smile at someone new first, and tell them your name.
rising.reversed:
Scorpio rising with this card reversed can look like a locked gate. You're polite and private and nobody gets any further, and after a while people stop trying. Venus in detriment on your Ascendant makes the warmth freeze on the way out, and the pull between the card's fire and your sign's water can make any friendliness feel fake to you. Some of that is protection. By now some of it is habit.

Colleagues respect you and don't invite you to things. You might have lived somewhere a year and still not know the neighbours' names. On dates the guard can read as disinterest. At a party you might spend the whole night by the kitchen bench with the one person you already knew. Say yes to one invitation you'd normally turn down, and stay long enough to have one proper conversation.

sun.upright:
Sagittarius Suns are proud of how far they've gone. The trips, the ideas, the friends in four countries, the version of yourself you became by leaving somewhere. Mutable fire, ruled by Jupiter. This is a homecoming card, which might sound like the opposite of all that, but the astrology is friendly. Aries trines Sagittarius, the same element four signs apart, and things flow easily between them. Venus has no dignity in your sign and takes on Jupiter's big, generous manner.

So this is homecoming the Sagittarius way. A party that spills out into the street. A table with room for whoever turns up, including the person you met on the bus. Home for you is often people more than a place. Doubled fire amplifies, which is lovely and also a bit risky, because your Sun already struggles with staying. When somewhere starts to feel settled you can feel the itch to be off, and the card is asking whether this time you might stay for the good part. Temperance is your sign's Major, an angel pouring water between two cups without spilling any, and that's roughly what a Sagittarius needs here, a way to have the roots and the road.

At work it's a team that feels like a travelling band, and a milestone worth throwing a proper do for. With friends it might be a reunion. It could be coming home after a long time away. Put down one root you'll have to come back to, a lease, a club, a garden bed, and keep it going.
sun.reversed:
For a Sagittarius Sun, the reversed Four often looks like leaving just as it gets good. The job was finally settled, the flat finally furnished, the friendships finally deep, and you're reading about somewhere else. Jupiter rules your Sun and makes it sound like growth. Sometimes it is. Sometimes it's that staying put makes you nervous in a way you'd prefer not to look at.

It shows in a string of places that almost became home, and in friends who are fond of you and don't expect you to be around for long. At work it's moving on before the project you started gets its moment. The trine with Aries makes going feel light and natural. Before you book anything, stay put for one more season and see what the place is like once the newness wears off.

moon.upright:
A Sagittarius Moon needs room. It settles when there's a bit of sky, a plan for the weekend, a sense that it could leave if it wanted to. Jupiter rules your Moon and makes the feelings big and hopeful. For your tides this card is about home and gathering, and you might expect it to feel close. It mostly doesn't. Aries trines Sagittarius, both fire, and Venus in your Moon's sign borrows Jupiter's style, so the belonging this card offers you is roomy and warm and full of people who don't ask you to stay in every night.

What you'll recognise is how good you feel around warm, funny, optimistic company, and how fast you sink in a house where everyone's tense. The doubled fire makes the good moods big, the kind of evening that turns into a trip. The flip side is that when things get a bit dull or close, you can read it as being trapped and want out, when staying would actually do more for you.

It shows with friends, maybe a group trip, or a night that starts as dinner and ends at three in the morning. It shows with family, where you might feel more at ease than usual, or where the old itch to leave is back. Your body gets restless after too many nights in, and sleeps better after a day outdoors. Have people round on a weeknight, and let it be ordinary.
moon.reversed:
Closeness starts to look like a fence to a Sagittarius Moon when this card is reversed. Someone wants a bit more of you and you're suddenly planning a trip. A home that's getting settled makes you edgy, and you fill the feeling with bookings and big ideas. Jupiter rules your Moon and can make escape look like optimism.

It tends to show in relationships that end just as they deepen, and in a lot of plans for elsewhere when you're low. The body gets restless, poor sleep, too many late nights. Friends may joke that you're impossible to pin down, and under the joke they've stopped expecting you. Stay through the next dull patch with someone you care about, and notice that you're still free.

rising.upright:
Sagittarius rising meets people wide open. Jupiter rules your chart, and strangers usually take you for friendly, frank, up for anything, the one who'll suggest the second bar. Drawn for your mask, the Four of Wands turns that friendliness into a proper welcome. You're inviting people as well as chatting to them, folding strangers into whatever you've got going on, the trip, the dinner, the group.

The astrology helps. Aries trines Sagittarius in the same element, and doubled fire is quick and bright, so you're likely to come across as warmer and more generous than even you usually do. Venus picks up Jupiter's big style in your sign. The risk with all that openness is that it's broad and not very deep. You might meet thirty people at a wedding, have a lovely time with every one of them, and never see any of them again. Sagittarius rising is good at beginnings. The follow-up is what tends to slip.

Starting somewhere new, you'll be the one inviting people for Friday drinks. Travelling, you'll likely end up at someone's house for dinner within a day of arriving. Dating is fun and easy. Pick one person you've warmed to and actually follow up, a message, a plan, within a few days.
rising.reversed:
A reversed Four makes Sagittarius rising all welcome and no follow-through. You invite everyone to everything, and then you're off somewhere else and the invitations stay vague. People feel warmly received and then slightly forgotten. Jupiter rules your chart and promises big. Your frankness can land harder than you mean, too, a joke at a party that someone takes home with them.

In a new town you might be popular and not really known by anybody. Colleagues enjoy you and don't rely on you. Dating is a lot of great first dates. Some of it is that staying in one conversation feels like missing another. Choose one invitation you've made loosely and turn it into a real one, with a time and a place.

sun.upright:
Capricorn Suns measure themselves by what they've built. Cardinal earth, ruled by Saturn, you're proud of the thing that took ten years, the house paid down, the business still standing, the reputation earned the slow way. The Four of Wands is a card about the day the building's done and people come to see it. You'd think that would suit you, and it does, sort of. The trouble is getting you to stop long enough to have the day.

The card's sign, Aries, squares Capricorn. Both are cardinal signs, both used to leading, and a square is friction that forces something to move. Aries wants the party now. Capricorn wants to finish the next stage first, and then the one after that. Fire and earth aren't enemies, they just haven't been introduced. Venus is a visitor in Capricorn with no dignity there, and she takes on Saturn's colour, so even the warmth feels a bit dutiful, the celebration you'll allow once everything's signed off. I've seen a lot of Capricorns get to the top of something and find they've forgotten how to enjoy it. The Devil is your sign's Major, and one of the things it chains people to is work.

At work this is a milestone, a promotion, a big contract, a business anniversary, and it deserves a real celebration. With family it might be the house, or a parent who'd like to be thanked. With a partner it's making time for an occasion you'd usually skip. Book the dinner for the milestone you just passed, before the next one arrives.
sun.reversed:
Capricorn Suns with the Four reversed often miss the milestone entirely. You hit the target and moved the target. There's always one more stage before it's worth celebrating, and Saturn is very good at making rest look like laziness. Or you do celebrate, and it's stiff, a work do that feels like work. The square with Aries turns the urge to celebrate into impatience with anyone who wants to stop.

It shows in a career that looks great from outside and feels like a treadmill from inside, and at home, where people have stopped expecting you at things. A partner might have given up planning anniversaries. Your body carries some of it, in the shoulders and the jaw. Put the next celebration in your calendar the way you'd book a meeting, and go to it.

moon.upright:
A Capricorn Moon feels safest when it's got things covered. Bills paid, plans made, nobody owed anything. Saturn rules your Moon and tends to make you self-sufficient early, and needing people can feel a bit like failing. The Four of Wands asks you to be looked after, to sit in a warm room with people who are glad you're there and not organise anything. That's a stretch. Aries squares Capricorn, the kind of angle that forces a change, and Venus in your Moon's sign takes on Saturn's reserve, so warmth reaches you slowly and has to prove itself first.

Underneath, you probably want this more than you let on. Capricorn Moons often grew up being the sensible one, and a home where someone else handles dinner can bring up an odd mix of relief and discomfort. Fire and earth don't clash, so there's no fight to have, you just have to let the warmth in deliberately. Once you do, it lasts. You don't do belonging quickly, and you don't lose it quickly either.

It shows at home, maybe in a house that finally feels settled after years of work. It shows in the body, as tension held in the upper back that lets go around the right people. With family it might be a parent or sibling offering help, and you not knowing what to do with it. Let someone cook for you, and don't wash up afterwards.
moon.reversed:
With the Four reversed, a Capricorn Moon can shut the need away entirely and call it coping. You provide, you manage, you're fine. Everyone relies on you and you rely on nobody, and the celebrations you organise for other people feel like jobs. Saturn's reserve and the square with Aries turn any unmet feeling into more work.

It shows in a home you keep running and never rest in, and in family occasions where you're the one making it happen. The body carries it too, the back, the sleep that never quite refreshes. Part of you may be a bit proud of how little you need, and that's worth noticing. Ask someone for help with something you could easily do yourself, and let them do it their way.

rising.upright:
Capricorn rising looks like someone in charge. Saturn rules your chart, and new people tend to read you as capable, composed, a bit formal, the person they'd go to if the power went out. Warmth isn't usually the first thing people notice. With this card drawn for your mask, it might be. The card asks you to lead with a welcome, and that isn't your normal order. Respect first, then warmth, is more the Capricorn rising way.

Aries squares Capricorn, and both are cardinal, so there's friction and also energy in this. You might notice you're quicker to be friendly than usual, more willing to go first. Earth and fire need introducing, so the warmth has to be brought into your style deliberately, and when it is, people tend to find it very reassuring. A welcome from someone who clearly doesn't hand them out to everyone feels like it means something. Venus in Capricorn takes on Saturn's manner, which keeps it dignified.

For a manager, or anyone meeting a new team, a bit of warmth makes your competence easier to be around. At a family event you might be the one hosting, and doing it well. In dating it helps to show interest earlier than you'd normally allow. Say something warm and personal in the first five minutes of the next meeting, before any business.
rising.reversed:
Composure can turn into a closed door when this card is upside down on Capricorn rising. You come across as competent and a bit cold, and people assume you'd prefer to be left alone. Saturn rules your chart and likes control, and the square from Aries can have you pushing, managing, running the room when a simple hello was all anyone wanted.

Colleagues respect you and don't ask you to the pub. You end up running gatherings you were only meant to attend. A first date can feel like an interview. It can show with neighbours you've known for years and still call by their surnames. Venus is only a visitor in your sign, and here she's gone very quiet. Let someone see you laugh at yourself, early on, and skip the agenda.

sun.upright:
Aquarius Suns want to belong on their own terms. Fixed air, ruled by Saturn and in modern astrology Uranus, you're proud of thinking for yourself, and you tend to find your people through ideas and causes and shared oddities more than through family or postcode. The Four of Wands and Aquarius get on. Aries sextiles your sign, a friendly angle, and air keeps fire going. The card's warmth catches easily on your circles and networks.

There's a cooler note, too. Venus has no dignity in Aquarius and picks up Saturn's reserve, and she also rules the first ten degrees of your sign, the Five of Swords, a card about the fallout when a group turns on someone. You might know that feeling. A lot of Aquarians have a story about the group that didn't want them, and it can leave you standing a little outside even the gatherings you love, part of it and watching it at the same time. The sextile helps, but only if you use it. It's an open door, and you have to decide to walk in and stay.

At work it's a team or project that's become something you actually care about, and a moment to mark it together. With friends it's the chosen family, the misfits who became your people. In a community group or a cause, it might be an anniversary or a win. Go to the next gathering of your people and stay until the end, stacking the chairs.
sun.reversed:
An Aquarius Sun with the Four reversed can belong to everything in theory and nothing in practice. You're in the group chats, you believe in the cause, you know everyone, and you've kept yourself carefully at the edge of all of it. Saturn's reserve makes the distance feel like integrity. The Five of Swords in your sign can make you half expect to be let down.

Friends would like to be closer to you and aren't sure how. In groups you're the commentator more than a member. Uranus, the modern ruler, adds a streak of wanting to be different even from people who like you. It can show at family gatherings too. Join in with something the group does without analysing it first, and let people see you enjoy it.

moon.upright:
An Aquarius Moon needs space to feel safe. Friendly company, interesting conversation, people who don't ask you to have your feelings on cue. Too much closeness too fast and you go cool. The Four of Wands offers a crowd and a garland, which is fine by you as long as nobody clings. Aries sextiles Aquarius, and fire and air are on good terms, so group warmth reaches you easily. Venus has no rank in Aquarius and picks up Saturn's reserve, and what soothes you is roomy, unpossessive company, the kind of friends who can go months without talking and pick straight back up.

The complication is the Five of Swords. Venus rules the opening decan of Aquarius, and that card is about a group that's turned sour. A lot of Aquarius Moons carry some memory of being on the outside of a circle, and it shows up as a small, careful distance, even with people you love. You might enjoy a gathering and still find yourself watching it from the corner of the room. That isn't exactly a flaw. It's how you keep yourself safe. The card is suggesting it might be safe enough, this time, to come in a bit further.

It shows with friends, maybe a group you're growing closer to. It shows at home if you share it, where some space of your own matters a lot. It shows with family, where big emotional scenes send you into your head. Tell a friend you missed them, in those words.
moon.reversed:
Detachment becomes armour for an Aquarius Moon when this card is reversed. Someone gets close and you go analytical. A friend has a crisis and you give good advice from a long way off. Venus with Saturn's reserve, and the Five of Swords in your sign, can convince you a group will let you down, so you never quite let it hold you.

It shows in friendships that stay pleasant and shallow, and in a partnership where you're asked for more feeling than you're comfortable showing. At home you might retreat into your room, or your head. The loneliness can be real, even among people who like you. Stay in a conversation about feelings for five minutes longer than you want to, and don't change the subject.

rising.upright:
Aquarius rising makes an odd first impression, in a good way. You come across as friendly and slightly detached, a bit unusual, hard to put in a box. Saturn rules your chart, Uranus in the modern version. With the Four of Wands on your mask, the friendliness is warmer than usual. You're pulling people in, especially the ones who don't quite fit anywhere else, and they'll often feel they've found their crowd.

The card helps. Aries sextiles Aquarius, and fire lifts air, so you're coming across as bright and open and easy to join. Venus picks up Saturn's colour in your sign, which keeps the warmth unfussy. People can relax around you because you're not asking much of them. The Five of Swords, Venus's decan at the start of Aquarius, adds a small guard. You welcome widely and trust carefully, and some people will notice they've been invited in and then kept at a certain distance.

At a party you're the one who introduces the new person to the interesting people. At work you might be the reason a group of colleagues becomes an actual social group. In dating it's friendly and fun, and the other person may need a signal that it's more than friendly. Next time you like someone, tell them plainly.
rising.reversed:
Fascinating and out of reach is how Aquarius rising can come across with the card reversed. People enjoy meeting you and leave feeling they only met the interesting surface. Saturn's reserve and the wariness of the Five of Swords keep you a step outside, even at your own gathering.

Colleagues like you and find you hard to know. On dates your cool can read as not interested. In groups you may notice you always stand near the door. In a new city it can mean lots of acquaintances and nobody you'd ring at midnight. Uranus likes to keep its options open, and people can feel that. Let someone see an ordinary, unclever side of you, and stay in the middle of the room for a while.

sun.upright:
Venus is exalted in Pisces. That's an old way of saying she's an honoured guest there, at her most tender and idealistic, and when a Pisces Sun draws the Four of Wands the card's planet is about as welcome as it ever gets. Mutable water, ruled by Jupiter and in modern astrology Neptune, you want to be proud of a life that means something, and a lot of that meaning comes through the people you love and the feeling of being part of something bigger than yourself.

The card itself belongs to Aries, which sits right next to Pisces on the wheel, the start of the zodiac beside the end of it, two neighbours with very little in common. And the card is fire, where you're water. So the warmth in this card suits you completely. The way it arrives is another matter. It's quick, loud, organised, a party with a start time. You'd probably prefer something quieter, a long dinner that runs late, a homecoming you can feel in your chest. Both are on offer. You might find yourself moved at the gathering in a way that surprises people.

At work it might be a team that's become close, and you're likely the one who makes it feel like family. With friends and family, a reunion or a wedding can hit you harder than most. In creative work or a spiritual practice, it's a sense of having arrived somewhere. When you're invited to something, say what kind of evening you'd actually enjoy.
sun.reversed:
For a Pisces Sun, the reversed Four can mean giving yourself away at every gathering. You're everyone's soft landing, the friend who listens at the party, and you go home with no idea what you wanted. Or the celebration you imagined was so perfect that the real one, with its noise and its awkward relatives, lets you down. Venus exalted can idealise things past the point any actual event could match.

It shows at family occasions, at work where you hold the team's mood together, and in love, where you can lose track of yourself in a partner. Escaping, into a screen or a drink or a daydream, can creep in. Before the next gathering, decide one thing you want from it, and make sure you get it.

moon.upright:
A Pisces Moon soaks up rooms. You walk in and know within a minute who's upset, who's pretending, who needs a glass of water, and a lot of that ends up living in your body for the rest of the evening. Jupiter rules Pisces, Neptune in the modern version, and the feelings are wide and a bit boundless. The Four of Wands for your tides offers a gathering, and with Venus exalted in your Moon's sign, the tender side of the card reaches you at full strength. Being loved by a group of people can undo a lot of loneliness for you.

The friction is elemental. The card is fire and your Moon is water, and a loud, busy celebration can swamp you even when you love everyone in it. Aries sits right next to Pisces and has little in common with it. So you'll probably find the card's promise lands best in a gentler form, a small dinner, a few people who know you, a room with soft light and nobody performing. The Moon is Pisces's Major, a card of things half-seen by moonlight, and belonging for you can feel almost dreamlike when it's right.

It shows in sleep and energy, restored by gentle company and wrecked by chaotic company. It shows with family, where you may feel everyone's mood at once. It shows with a partner, in how much you need quiet time together. Keep the next gathering small, and leave before you're drained.
moon.reversed:
When this card is reversed, a Pisces Moon can lose itself in everyone else's needs and forget its own. You go to the thing, absorb every mood in the room, and come home empty. Or you drift away from real gatherings into a fantasy of the perfect one, and nothing actual lives up to it. Venus exalted makes the ideal very bright.

It shows in exhaustion after social things, in sleep that doesn't restore you, and in escaping into a screen or a glass of wine. The fire in the card and the water in you can leave you foggy after a busy week. With family you might feel flooded. Name one thing you need from the next person you see, even something tiny, and ask for it.

rising.upright:
Pisces rising takes on the colour of whoever's in the room. Strangers tend to find you gentle, kind, a bit hard to pin down, someone they tell things to without quite meaning to. Jupiter rules your chart, and Neptune in modern astrology. The Four of Wands for your mask turns all that softness into a welcome, and because Venus is exalted in Pisces, the warmth people meet in you is unguarded and generous. People feel understood around you, often within minutes.

Aries, the card's sign, sits just before Pisces with little in common, and its fire meets your water, so the card's brisk hosting energy doesn't quite fit your style. You welcome people by tuning into them, working out what they need and offering it. The card might be nudging you to be a little more direct about it, to actually say come in, sit down, stay. That can feel unnatural for Pisces rising. It also saves people a lot of guessing.

At a party you're the one the shy person ends up talking to. At work, people bring you their troubles, sometimes more of them than you'd like. In dating you can come across as very open, which is lovely, as long as the other person's worth it. Next time you meet someone new, tell them one plain fact about yourself they didn't ask for.
rising.reversed:
Pisces rising can turn into whatever the other person wants when the Four is reversed. You mirror, you soften, you welcome by disappearing a bit, and afterwards people have a lovely impression of someone they couldn't describe. Venus exalted can also make you see the best in everyone you meet, until they let you down.

At work you take on everyone's feelings and burn out quietly. On dates you match the other person so well they never meet you. In new friendships it can mean saying yes to plans you don't want. The fire and water between the card and your sign leave you drained after social things. Say one thing you disagree with, gently, the next time you're getting to know someone.

1.upright:
The first house is the body and the way you begin things. Its natural sign is Aries and its natural ruler is Mars, and this card comes from Aries as well, its last ten degrees, so it's standing on its own ground here. It's an angular house, one of the four corners of the chart, so whatever's going on tends to show quickly, in your face, your energy, how you walk into a room. What's live is a warmer, more sociable version of you. You might be starting things with other people in mind, looking for company, making an effort with how you present.

There's friction built in, though. Venus is in detriment in Aries, which means she has to work against the grain in the very sign this house belongs to. So the warmth is real and it comes out at Mars speed. You're friendly fast, generous fast, keen for everyone to get on, and you may notice you've invited people into something before it's properly started. The card and the house are both fire, which turns the volume up. Mercury has its joy in the first house too, so a lot of it comes out through talk, the quick joke, the introduction.

In the body it might be more energy around people and less on your own, and a new interest in how you look. In a new start, a job or a move, it's the urge to make it social early. In how people see you, it's warmer and more approachable than usual. Before you launch the next new thing, get its foundations sorted, then invite people in.
1.reversed:
In the first house, the reversed Four often shows up as starting things too fast and not feeling at home in any of them. You begin with a lot of warmth and noise, the new job, the new gym, the new friendship, and a month later you're somewhere else. Venus struggles in the house's own sign, and doubled fire burns through a beginning quickly.

It shows in the body as restlessness, or running hot and then tired. It shows in how you present, a bright front that doesn't match how unsettled you feel. People may see someone confident when you feel adrift. Mars rules this house and never minds a fresh start. Pick one thing you've started recently and stick with it through the dull part before you begin anything else.

2.upright:
Money and self-worth live in the second house, along with the things you own and what you think you deserve. Venus is the house's natural ruler, so the Four of Wands is on home turf here, and its planet has real say over this part of your life. Taurus is the natural sign, fixed earth, and the house is succedent, which means it builds up and holds on. What's live is money connected to people. Spending on a gathering, a home, a wedding, a shared meal. A sense of your own worth that's tied to what you can offer others.

The friction is between the card's sign and the house's. Aries is Taurus's neighbour on the wheel, and the two have very little in common, and fire and earth need to be introduced before they'll work together. So the Aries side of this card wants to spend on the celebration, and the Taurus side of the house wants to know it's affordable. You might notice both pulls around the same time. The generous impulse is a good one, and it's worth checking against the bank balance before you act on it.

With income it might be a pay rise or a finished job that deserves marking. With spending it's putting money into your home or your people, which can be very good for you. With self-worth it's feeling valued because of how you look after others, which is lovely, and also worth watching. Set a budget for the next celebration and stick to it, then enjoy it without guilt.
2.reversed:
Money spent on the party before the foundations are there is a common shape for the reversed Four in the second house. The celebration, the house, the gifts, all a bit ahead of what the account can carry. Venus rules this house and likes nice things, and the Aries hurry pushes the spending forward. Sometimes it runs the other way, and you won't spend anything on joy at all.

It shows on the credit card statement after a big occasion, and in self-worth that wobbles when you can't be the generous one. It can show in a home you've spent a lot on and still don't feel settled in.
