Look at what you spent on celebrations and gatherings over the last few months, write it down, and decide what was worth it.

3.upright:
The third house is the everyday stuff. Messages, phone calls, the neighbourhood, siblings and cousins, the short trips and the evening classes. It's a cadent house, where things get learned and passed along. With this card here, a lot of warmth is running through ordinary contact. Aries sextiles Gemini, the house's natural sign, a cooperative angle, and fire and air suit each other, so the card's energy moves quickly through words and small gatherings.

That might look like the family group chat getting friendlier, a sibling you've been distant from ringing out of the blue, the street party somebody finally organises. You might be the somebody. The Moon has its joy in this house, which makes it homely, the neighbour who drops round with lemons, the regular coffee with the same person. A sextile is an opening, not a guarantee, so a lot depends on whether you actually send the message you've been writing in your head.

With siblings it could be a reunion, or a milestone in their life you're asked to be part of. In your local area it's getting to know people, becoming a regular somewhere. In learning, a short course might come with good company. Send the invitation you've been meaning to send, with a date in it.
3.reversed:
A reversed Four in the third house can mean plenty of cheerful noise and very little actual contact. The family chat is full of emojis and nobody's said anything real in months. Plans with neighbours or siblings keep getting floated and dropped. Sometimes there's friction under the chatter, something unresolved with a brother or sister that everyone's being polite about.

It shows in messages, the ones you haven't answered and the ones you keep light on purpose. It shows with the neighbours, where you wave and don't know their names. It can show in a course you started keenly and quietly stopped going to. Mercury rules this house and can keep things very busy and very shallow. Ring one sibling or old friend, and talk for longer than ten minutes.

4.upright:
Home is the fourth house. The actual house or flat, the family you grew up in, the private ground you go back to. It's angular, one of the four corners of the chart, so what happens here sets the tone for everything else. This card is all homecoming, garlands on the front gate, and on the surface it's a perfect match. The astrology is more mixed. Aries squares Cancer, the natural sign of this house, and the card's fire runs straight into the house's water.

What that tends to feel like is wanting a home that's both lively and safe, and finding the two pull against each other. You might want to throw the doors open, have everyone round, celebrate a move or a new baby or a renovation finished. Then the house fills up and someone's upset, or it's too loud, or you realise the family needed a quiet week and you gave them a party. The Moon is this house's natural ruler and it runs on feeling, and the card's Aries fire can rush it.

In the home itself it might be a move, an extension, finally unpacking the last boxes. With family it could be a reunion, or making peace with a parent enough to celebrate something together. With the people you live with, it's working out how much company everyone actually wants. Ask your household what they'd like to celebrate, and plan it around their answer.
4.reversed:
The fourth house with the Four reversed is often a home that won't settle. You've moved and it doesn't feel like yours yet. Or the family looks fine from outside and there's tension at every dinner. The square from Aries makes the friction flare, and fire meeting water leaves everyone steamed up and tired. The Moon rules this house, and when home is off, your moods follow.

It shows in a house you're between more than in, a lease running out, a renovation dragging on. It shows with parents or siblings, in a gathering you're dreading. It can show as not wanting to go home at the end of the day. Fix one small thing in the house that's bothered you for months, and sort out one small thing with someone who lives in it.

5.upright:
The fifth house is play. Romance, creativity, children, parties, anything you do for fun. Venus has her joy here, which means the card's planet does its best work in exactly this part of the chart. Add that Aries trines Leo, the house's natural sign, both of them fire, and you have one of the happiest placements this card can get. It's a succedent house, so what you enjoy here tends to build up over time.

What's live is delight that wants company. A romance you'd like to show off. Something you've made that deserves an audience. A child's milestone, a birthday party, a first date that turns into a whole weekend. Doubled fire amplifies, and most of the time that's lovely. The too-much version is the party that costs more than it should, or a new romance rushed along because the spark was so good you didn't want to wait.

In love it might be a proper date night, an anniversary, a relationship going public. With children it's play and celebration, the kind of birthday they'll remember. In creative work it's finishing something and sharing it, the exhibition, the gig, the dinner where you cook the dish you've been practising. Plan one evening purely for fun, invite the people who make you laugh, and don't make it useful.
5.reversed:
Reversed in the fifth house, the Four can mean fun that's been scheduled out of existence. The date nights have stopped, the creative project is in the cupboard, the kids' party was organised to the minute and nobody enjoyed it, including you. Venus has her joy here, so when she's blocked the whole house goes flat. The trine with Leo makes fun come easily, which is partly why it's so noticeable when it's gone.

It can also be the opposite, a romance rushed past the point of knowing each other, or a celebration put on mostly for the photos. It shows in weekends that feel like work, and in a partner who's asked when you last did something together just for fun. Book something frivolous, a gig, a class, a day at the beach, and go.

6.upright:
The sixth house is the daily round. Your job as you actually do it each day, the routines that keep you going, the body's upkeep, the dishes and the dog walk. A card about milestones and parties has landed in a house of daily routine, which isn't its natural habitat. Venus is in fall in Virgo, the house's natural sign, uncomfortable and having to find an indirect way to do her job. Aries quincunxes Virgo as well, an angle of constant small adjustments.

So the warmth comes in small, practical forms. Lunch with colleagues. A good team. The cup of tea someone brings you mid-morning. Fire and earth need introducing, and the card is asking you to introduce them, to put some pleasure and company into the ordinary run of the day. Mars has its joy in the sixth house, and Mars rules Aries, the card's own sign, so there's real energy here, the kind that likes a physical job done alongside other people. A shared project at work, a running group, a community garden.

At work it might be a team finally gelling, or a small win worth marking with more than an email. In the body it's energy that lifts when you're around people, and a routine that goes better with company. With your daily habits it's making them pleasant enough to keep. Find one part of your working day you can share with someone, and make it a regular thing.
6.reversed:
In the sixth house, the reversed Four tends to show as a daily grind with nothing warm in it. Work is tasks and more tasks, lunch is at the desk, the routines are all duty. Venus in fall here has trouble getting any pleasure in, and the quincunx keeps you making small adjustments that never quite fix it.

It shows in the body as a low, steady tiredness, and at work as a team that doesn't feel like one. Mars has its joy in this house, and when it's frustrated it can come out as irritation with colleagues. Sometimes the problem is at home, and it drains you before the working day has even started. Eat lunch with someone at least twice a week, away from the screen, and see what it does to your afternoons.

7.upright:
The seventh house is the person opposite you. A partner, a spouse, a business partner, anyone you've made a serious one-to-one agreement with. Venus is its natural ruler, so this card is on home ground here, and a card about weddings, moving in and making it official has landed in exactly the house where those things live. It's angular, so what happens here tends to be visible, and it tends to matter.

The interesting part is the axis. The card's sign is Aries and the house's natural sign is Libra, directly opposite. Aries is the natural sign of the first house, the self, and Libra of the seventh, the other person, so the card brings your side of the axis into their house. There's a pull between what you want and what the partnership wants. You might be ready to celebrate, to commit, to move in, and need to check the other person is at the same point. Fire and air keep each other going, so the energy between you stays warm and quick.

In a relationship this might be an engagement, a wedding, moving in, meeting the family. In a business partnership it's a contract signed or a joint milestone worth marking. It could also be meeting someone new who's warm and direct and wants to get on with it. Ask your partner what milestone they'd like to mark next, and listen to the whole answer before you offer yours.
7.reversed:
A partnership milestone that's out of step is the usual story when the Four lands reversed in the seventh house. One of you wants to move in and the other isn't ready. The wedding's being planned and it feels like a project. Or things look settled from outside and feel thin between the two of you. The Aries opposition means one person's drive can run ahead of the other's.

Venus rules this house, so when things sour here they tend to hurt. It shows in who's pushing for the next step, and in whether you both actually want it. In business it can be a partnership that looked good and is starting to strain. Have the conversation about pace, plainly, before the next commitment gets made.

8.upright:
The eighth house holds what you share at the deepest level. Joint money, debts, inheritances, the mortgage with two names on it, and intimacy, sex included. Endings live here too. The Four of Wands isn't comfortable in this house. Venus is at a disadvantage in Scorpio, the eighth's natural sign, in detriment and working against the grain. Aries quincunxes Scorpio, with no common ground, and the card's fire meets the house's water. A bright, public celebration card has landed in the most private part of the chart.

What that can feel like is wanting to mark something deep and not knowing how. Merging finances with a partner. Paying off a debt. Settling an estate. A relationship that's become truly intimate. These are milestones, but they aren't the kind you throw a party for. Mars rules both Aries and Scorpio in the traditional system, so there's a shared ruler under the friction, and some real heat. Closeness in this house can be intense and very warm once it gets going.

With joint money it's a good time to sort things out together and mark it, even quietly, a dinner once the accounts are merged. In intimacy it's warmth and trust going deeper. With an inheritance or an ending, it's honouring what's closing. Choose a private way to mark something that matters to you and one other person, and keep it between the two of you.
8.reversed:
In the eighth house the reversed Four tends to mean closeness that stays near the surface. Shared money looks fine and nobody's actually talked about it. Intimacy happens and doesn't feel close. Venus in detriment and the clash of fire with water make it hard for the card's warmth to get down to where it's needed.

It shows in joint finances celebrated too early, the new house bought before the budget was really discussed. It shows in a partner who feels a bit far away even when you're together, and sometimes in an ending you haven't let yourself grieve. It can also be a family inheritance that's turned awkward. Sit down with the person you share money with and go through it all, the debts included.

9.upright:
Travel, study and belief belong to the ninth house, along with publishing, philosophy and anything that takes you well past your usual streets. The Sun has its joy here, and the natural sign is Sagittarius, ruled by Jupiter. The Four of Wands travels well into this house. Aries trines Sagittarius, the same element four signs apart, and with fire on both sides the whole thing is warm and expansive.

What's live might be a homecoming from far away, or a celebration that brings people together across distance. A graduation. A wedding overseas. A friend from another country coming to stay. You might also find meaning showing up through people, a sense that the ones you gather around you are part of what you believe in. The too-much side of all this fire is the urge to keep going, always the next trip, the next course, and never quite settling into what you've found.

In study it's finishing something, a degree or a qualification, and letting yourself mark it. In travel it's the trip that feels like going home, or the one that brings you back to your people. With in-laws or relatives far away it can be a warmer connection than usual. Plan a proper celebration for something you learned or finished, and ask along the people who helped you get there.
9.reversed:
Reversed in the ninth house, the Four can turn into homesickness for somewhere you haven't found yet. You keep looking at courses, flights, places to move, and the life you're actually living doesn't feel like it counts. The trine makes leaving look easy, and all that fire keeps the itch going. Jupiter rules this house, and it always thinks the next place will be bigger and better.

It shows in study that never quite gets finished, and in travel used to avoid a home that feels unsettled. Beliefs can get restless too, one philosophy after another and nothing that sticks. It can show with relatives overseas, a visit that keeps getting put off. Pick one thing about where you live that you'd miss if you left, and spend more time with it.

10.upright:
Career sits at the top of the chart, in the tenth house, along with your public role and what people know you for. It's angular, so it's visible. The Four of Wands here is a public milestone, a promotion, a launch, an award, a business anniversary, the moment your work gets seen. Capricorn is the house's natural sign, ruled by Saturn, and Aries squares Capricorn, both cardinal, both wanting to lead.

That square is the tension to know about. Aries wants to celebrate the moment something's done. Capricorn and Saturn want it proven first, built to last, checked twice. Fire and earth have to be introduced before they'll cooperate. So you might be pulled between marking a professional win and worrying it's too soon, and both instincts have something to them. Saturn would say a reputation lasts longer when the work under it is solid. Aries would say nobody ever got promoted for keeping quiet about a good result.

At work this might be a promotion, a new role, a team milestone you're leading. In your reputation it's being known as someone who brings people together and gives credit. If you run your own business, it could be an anniversary or a launch. Mark the next professional milestone publicly, once you're sure it's finished, and thank the people who got you there by name.
10.reversed:
The tenth house with the Four reversed can mean a public celebration ahead of the actual achievement. The launch before the product works. The announcement before the contract's signed. Your name on something that isn't ready. The Aries square pushes for the milestone before Saturn is happy with it, and people notice the gap.

It can also be the reverse, a real achievement nobody's recognised, including your boss. Fire and earth never got properly introduced, so the celebrating and the building are running at different speeds. It shows in a career that looks shinier than it feels, and in work events where you feel like a fraud. Get the next thing properly finished and signed off, and then ask for the recognition you're owed.

11.upright:
The eleventh house is your wider circle. Friends, networks, clubs, the online groups, and the hopes you have for the future. Jupiter has its joy here, which makes it a generous part of the chart. Drawn into the eleventh, this card turns friendship into something like family. Aries sextiles Aquarius, the house's natural sign, and fire and air help each other, so the card's warmth spreads easily through groups.

That might look like a friend's wedding where you're more involved than usual, a group that's been loose for years suddenly getting organised, a community project reaching a milestone. You might be the one who hosts. The sextile is an easy opening that you still have to use. Saturn is the traditional ruler here, Uranus the modern one, and both bring a bit of distance to the eleventh, so the warmth may need someone to actually make the plan and send the invite.

With friends it's a gathering, a reunion, a trip together. In a club, team or community group it's a win or an anniversary worth marking. With your hopes, it might be a long-held wish that includes other people, the shared house, the group business. Host your friends for something simple, and ask one of them to help.
11.reversed:
Somebody always organises the catch-ups, and with the Four reversed in the eleventh house it's probably you, without feeling part of the group. You remember the birthdays, you book the table, and at the actual event you're on the edge of it. Or the circle itself has cooled, friends drifting, the group chat gone quiet.

It shows at friends' milestones you help with and don't enjoy, and in a network that's big on paper and thin in practice. Saturn's distance in this house makes it easy to hang back. Hopes for the future can start to feel like something you'll do on your own. Jupiter has its joy here, and it's happiest when the generosity runs both ways. Let someone else organise the next get-together, and just turn up.

12.upright:
The twelfth house is the hidden part of the chart. Sleep, retreat, the unconscious, the things you do in private and the things you don't quite admit. It's cadent, a house of processing and letting go. This is a public, festive card, so drawn here it has to go quiet. It is welcome, though. Venus is exalted in Pisces, the house's natural sign, which makes this a gentle, tender placement for the card's planet.

The friction is that the card is fire and the house is water, and Aries is the sign just before Pisces, a neighbour with little in common. So the celebrating turns inward. What's live might be a private sense of having arrived somewhere, a milestone nobody else knows about, recovery from something, a year since a loss. Saturn has its joy in this house, which suggests some structure helps, a regular retreat, a small ritual you keep. There can also be private generosity, help you give without anyone knowing, a celebration you organise for someone who needs it more than you do.

In sleep and rest it's a bedroom that feels like a sanctuary. In private life it's marking something that matters only to you. In caring roles it's warmth you give behind the scenes, in a hospital, a care home, at a friend's bedside. Mark one private milestone alone, in a way that feels right to you, and don't tell anyone.
12.reversed:
An unsettled feeling you can't name is often what the reversed Four brings to the twelfth house. Everything looks fine, and underneath you don't quite feel you belong anywhere. Venus exalted in this house's sign makes the loss of that inner warmth sharper. The fire and water between card and house can leave you foggy and tired.

It shows in sleep that doesn't refresh, in retreat that feels like hiding, and in private habits that numb more than they soothe. It can show as a quiet loneliness at gatherings. Saturn has its joy here, and a simple routine, the same bedtime, a daily walk alone, can help. Tell one person you trust that you've been feeling a bit lost, and let them keep you company.
